result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed SecurityConfig, all application logging, both production properties files, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, Oracle initialization files and Azure setup/reset scripts with credential literals redacted.

Database passwords require environment substitution; Oracle initializer requires environment passwords; SecurityConfig encodes an externally supplied admin password with BCrypt. .env.example contains explicit replacement placeholders, not deployed credentials. Azure setup uses environment values or cryptographic random password generation.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: Deletion is an authenticated, security-critical state change (SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain lines 54-56). DetailController.deletePhoto lines 64-76 records only the photo ID and outcome (line 69), and PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto lines 199-213 likewise logs only the photo ID. Neither method obtains or records the authenticated principal. Successful deletion audit records therefore omit the actor identity, preventing attribution of destructive actions to an authenticated account.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

notes: Repository-wide current-source assessment includes pre-existing code. Tests, generated code, .github/agents and historical Git revisions excluded. Static analysis only; deployment filesystem ACLs, actual runtime credentials and external log configuration were not observed.

Public gallery access is an explicit application design (SecurityConfig lines 19 and 57-58), not treated as an unintended resource permission. No confirmed incorrect explicit permission assignment found.
Actual credential literals are never reproduced. Missing actor identity in critical-event records is an auditability finding, not evidence that no logging exists.
